f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: An applicant can use an approach other than the one in this guidance if it satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss an alternative approach, the applicant can contact the FDA office responsible for the guidance as listed on the title page.
f.clause: Preamble (nonbinding statement)

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.quote: You can use an alternative approach if it satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations. To discuss an alternative approach, contact the FDA office responsible for this guidance as listed on the title page.
rows.location: Preamble (nonbinding statement)
rows.review_note: Review: statement reworded ('can contact') to match the permissive wording; boilerplate permission kept as Permitted. Double-check: Score 74: boilerplate alternative-approach statement; actor inferred from 'You', borderline as a PV requirement.

f.title: Use the PBRER in place of the PADER, PAER or PSUR to meet periodic reporting requirements
f.statement: Under the conditions described in the guidance, applicants can use the ICH E2C(R2) Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) format in place of the U.S. PADER, the U.S. PAER or the ICH E2C PSUR to satisfy the periodic postmarketing safety reporting requirements in 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2).
f.clause: I. Introduction
f.applicability: NDA, ANDA and BLA holders subject to 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2) or 600.80(c)(2)
f.systems: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; PADER; PAER; ICH E2C PSUR

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.quote: This guidance describes the conditions under which applicants 2 can use an alternative reporting format, the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) 3 E2C(R2) Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER), in place of the U.S. periodic adverse drug experience report (PADER), U.S. periodic adverse experience report (PAER), or ICH E2C Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR), to satisfy the periodic postmarketing safety reporting requirements in §§ 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2) (21 CFR 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2)).
rows.location: I. Introduction
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Overlaps with 0003 (FDA accepts PBRER); kept because 0002 frames the conditional use of the PBRER and 0003 the acceptance of all three formats. Double-check: merged 0003 (footnote 4: FDA accepts PADER/PAER, PSUR and PBRER) into this row as a true duplicate of the same permission; the footnote sentence is kept as lead-in in 0004's quote. Score 82: 'describes the conditions under which applicants can use' is descriptive framing, the conditions sit in sections III-V, and the quote carries footnote markers (2, 3).

f.title: Submit each periodic report format per its regulatory or ICH content and timelines
f.statement: Each periodic report format accepted under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2) (PADER/PAER, PSUR, PBRER) must be submitted according to the content and timelines specified in the regulations (PADER/PAER) or by ICH (PSUR and PBRER).
f.clause: I. Introduction (footnote 4)
f.systems: PADER; PAER; ICH E2C PSUR; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.deadline: Timelines specified in the regulations (PADER/PAER) or by ICH (PSUR and PBRER)
rows.quote: FDA accepts all three formats, the PADER/PAER, PSUR, and PBRER, to fulfill the postmarketing periodic safety reporting requirements under §§ 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2). Each format must be submitted according to the content and timelines specified in the regulations (PADER/PAER) or by ICH (PSUR and PBRER).
rows.location: I. Introduction (footnote 4)
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory confirmed - 'must' with the regulation (21 CFR 314.80(c)(2)/600.80(c)(2)) cited in the same footnote. For the PBRER, the ICH timelines referred to here are those reflected in 0034/0035 (70/90 days after the DLP). Double-check: level kept Mandatory because the footnote says 'must', but for the PSUR/PBRER the content and timelines come from ICH, not from a cited regulation, and the guidance is nonbinding; section V phrases the PBRER timelines (70/90 days, 0034/0035) as what the applicant 'can' do. Deadline is a cross-reference, not a fixed period. Footnote text. Score 75.

f.title: Submit postmarketing periodic safety reports for each approved application
f.statement: FDA regulations in 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2) require applicants to submit postmarketing periodic safety reports in the PADER/PAER format for each approved application.
f.clause: II.A. Postmarketing Periodic Safety Reporting Regulations
f.applicability: Each approved application
f.exceptions: Unless a waiver permits another format (see sections II.C and III)

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.quote: FDA regulations in §§ 314.80(c)(2) and 600.80(c)(2) require applicants to submit postmarketing periodic safety reports in the PADER/PAER format for each approved application.
rows.location: II.A. Postmarketing Periodic Safety Reporting Regulations
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory confirmed - quote cites the regulations that impose the duty. No change. Double-check: Score 88: quote proves the regulatory 'require' and actor, but it sits in the Background section and the exceptions field (waiver may permit another format) is drawn from II.C/III, not from this quote.

f.title: Submit periodic safety reports quarterly for 3 years after U.S. approval, then annually
f.statement: Postmarketing periodic safety reports must be submitted quarterly for the first 3 years following the U.S. approval date and annually thereafter.
f.clause: II.A. Postmarketing Periodic Safety Reporting Regulations
f.applicability: Each approved application (NDA, ANDA, BLA); restated in section III.B for PBRER waiver requests

rows.deadline: Quarterly for the first 3 years following the U.S. approval date; annually thereafter

rows.location: II.A. Postmarketing Periodic Safety Reporting Regulations
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory confirmed - quote cites 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2)(i)/600.80(c)(2)(i). No change. Double-check: merged 0026 (III.B: more than 3 years after approval, applicants must submit a periodic safety report annually under 314.80(c)(2)(i)/600.80(c)(2)(i)) into this row as a true duplicate of the annual part of the same regulatory duty. Quote proves the 'must', the actor (the reports of the applicant, previous sentence) and the cited sections; clock start (U.S. approval date) is explicit. Score 90 rather than higher because the subject 'The reports' relies on the preceding sentence.

f.title: Include the regulatory content in periodic safety reports
f.statement: Postmarketing periodic safety reports must contain the information described in 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2)(ii) and 600.80(c)(2)(ii).
f.clause: II.A. Postmarketing Periodic Safety Reporting Regulations

f.title: Submit all ICSRs electronically in a format FDA can process, review and archive
f.statement: All ICSRs must be submitted electronically in a format FDA can process, review and archive, as described in 21 CFR 314.80(g) and 600.80(h).
f.clause: II.C. Precedence for Granting PSUR Waivers
f.applicability: All ICSRs, including the nonexpedited ICSRs provided with periodic reports
f.systems: Electronic submission format FDA can process, review and archive

systems: Electronic submission format FDA can process, review and archive
rows.review_note: Review: kept as a current Mandatory duty - although listed among the historical PSUR waiver conditions in II.C, the sentence is a present-tense 'must' citing 21 CFR 314.80(g)/600.80(h). Double-check: Score 84: present-tense 'must' with 314.80(g)/600.80(h) in the quote, but the sentence sits inside a bullet describing historical PSUR-waiver conditions, so reading it as a standalone current duty is a judgement call.

f.title: Submit a PBRER instead of a PSUR under an existing PSUR waiver
f.statement: If an applicant already has a PSUR waiver for an approved application, FDA considers the existing waiver to permit submission of a PBRER instead of a PSUR under the conditions described; if the applicant substitutes the PBRER for the PSUR with no changes in the data lock point (DLP) or frequency of reporting, it can do so without submitting a new waiver request.
f.clause: III.A. Applicants With a PSUR Waiver
f.applicability: Applicants with an approved PSUR waiver
f.exceptions: Only where there is no change in the DLP or frequency of reporting
f.systems: ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; ICH E2C PSUR

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.quote: If applicants already have a PSUR waiver for an approved application, FDA will consider the existing PSUR waiver to permit applicants to submit a PBRER instead of a PSUR under the conditions described below, because the PBRER replaces the PSUR for postmarketing periodic safety reporting. If applicants wish to substitute the PBRER for the PSUR with no changes in the DLP or frequency of reporting, applicants can do so without submitting a new waiver request.
rows.location: III.A. Applicants With a PSUR Waiver
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed: quote proves the permission, actor and the no-change condition.

f.title: Submit a notification or new waiver request to change PSUR waiver conditions
f.statement: If an applicant wishes to change any condition of its PSUR waiver other than the format, it should submit either a notification or a new waiver request, depending on the circumstances described in sections III.A.1 to III.A.3.
f.clause: III.A. Applicants With a PSUR Waiver
f.applicability: Applicants with an approved PSUR waiver

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.quote: However, if applicants wish to change any conditions of their PSUR waiver other than the format, applicants should submit either a notification or new waiver request, depending on the circumstances described below.
rows.location: III.A. Applicants With a PSUR Waiver
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed: quote proves 'should', actor and condition; the circumstances are those of III.A.1-3 (cross-reference).

f.title: Ensure no reporting gaps when changing the DLP for the PBRER
f.statement: If an applicant wishes to use a DLP date for the PBRER that differs from the DLP date used for the PSUR, it should ensure there are no gaps in reporting intervals resulting from the change. Examples of appropriate alternatives are submitting overlapping reports, submitting a one-time PADER/PAER, or extending the reporting interval of the upcoming PADER/PAER by up to 3 months to cover the gap.
f.clause: III.A.1. Change in the Date of the DLP for the PBRER – Submit Notification
f.applicability: Applicants with a PSUR waiver changing the DLP for the PBRER

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)
rows.deadline: Extension of upcoming PADER/PAER interval limited to up to 3 months
rows.quote:
If applicants wish to use a DLP date for the PBRER that is different than the DLP date used for the PSUR, applicants should ensure there are no gaps in reporting intervals resulting from the change in DLP. Examples of appropriate alternatives include the following:

 • Submit overlapping reports to cover the gap.
 • Submit a one-time PADER/PAER to cover the gap.
 • Extend the reporting interval of the applicant’s upcoming PADER/PAER by up to 3 months to cover the gap.

f.title: Notify FDA in writing of a PBRER DLP change and gap-prevention measures
f.statement: Applicants should submit written notification to the application(s) indicating the change in DLP date and describing the measures taken to ensure that there are no resulting gaps in reporting.
f.clause: III.A.1. Change in the Date of the DLP for the PBRER – Submit Notification
f.applicability: Applicants with a PSUR waiver changing the DLP for the PBRER

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Score 88: quote proves 'should' and actor; applicability (PSUR-waiver holders changing the DLP) is taken from the section heading and context.

f.title: Submit PADER/PAER as needed to keep the waiver valid when filing the PBRER less often
f.statement: If an applicant wishes to submit the PBRER less frequently than permitted under its PSUR waiver, the continued validity of the waiver is conditioned on the applicant submitting a PADER/PAER as needed to fulfil the reporting frequency requirement under FDA regulations.
f.clause: III.A.2. Longer PBRER Reporting Intervals But No Change in Frequency – Submit Notification
f.applicability: Applicants with a PSUR waiver submitting the PBRER at longer intervals

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)

rows.location: III.A.2. Longer PBRER Reporting Intervals But No Change in Frequency – Submit Notification
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory kept - the regulatory reporting-frequency duty applies and the continued validity of the waiver is expressly conditioned on the PADER/PAER submissions; the quote refers to the requirement 'under our regulations' without a section number, so legal_basis now points to the frequency provisions cited in II.A. Title clarified. Double-check: legal_basis cleared: the quote cites no section ('our regulations' only). The Mandatory level rests on a waiver condition ('continued validity ... will be conditioned on'), not on a modal duty, so the level is a judgement call (it could equally be read as a condition of a permission). Score 58.

f.clause: III.A.2. Longer PBRER Reporting Intervals But No Change in Frequency – Submit Notification

f.title: Submit a new waiver request for other changes to PSUR waiver conditions
f.statement: If an applicant wishes to change any other condition of its PSUR waiver beyond a DLP change (III.A.1) or longer PBRER intervals (III.A.2), it should submit a new waiver request, for example to change the overall reporting frequency or to add or remove products covered by the report.
f.clause: III.A.3. Other Changes to the PSUR Waiver – Submit New Waiver
f.applicability: Applicants with a PSUR waiver

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)

For example, a new waiver request should be submitted to change the overall reporting frequency or to add or remove products covered by the report.
rows.location: III.A.3. Other Changes to the PSUR Waiver – Submit New Waiver
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed: quote proves 'should', actor, condition and examples.

f.title: Submit a waiver request before using the PBRER without a PSUR waiver
f.statement: If an applicant does not already have a PSUR waiver and wishes to submit in the PBRER format, a waiver request must be submitted under 21 CFR 314.90(a) or 600.90(a) in order to submit a PBRER instead of the PADER/PAER (PBRER waiver).
f.clause: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver
f.applicability: Applicants without a PSUR waiver

rows.location: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory confirmed - 'must be submitted under 314.90(a) or 600.90(a)'. No change. Double-check: confirmed: 'must be submitted under 314.90(a) or 600.90(a)' in the quote; actor and condition explicit.

f.title: Prepare a single PBRER for products with the same active moiety or ingredient
f.statement: In accordance with the ICH E2C(R2) PBRER guidance, applicants can prepare a single PBRER for multiple products with the same active moiety or ingredient.
f.clause: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver
f.applicability: Multiple products with the same active moiety or ingredient

rows.actor: Applicant (holder of an approved NDA, ANDA or BLA)

rows.location: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver

f.title: Use one waiver request letter referencing multiple applications
f.statement: If the waiver request is for several products, the applicant can submit a single waiver request letter that references multiple applications.
f.clause: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed: quote proves 'can', actor and condition.

f.title: Include product names, application numbers and an FDA contact in the PBRER waiver request
f.statement: Each PBRER waiver request should include the product name(s) and application number(s), and the email address and telephone number of the individual FDA may contact if the Agency needs additional information on the request.

f.title: Request a waiver of quarterly reporting in the first 3 years after U.S. approval
f.statement: Where the time from the product's U.S. approval date is 3 years or less, applicants can ask FDA to consider waiving the quarterly reporting requirement under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2)(i) and 600.80(c)(2)(i) and instead propose to submit the PBRER less frequently during this period (e.g., every 6 or 12 months); FDA grants or denies the request on an application-specific basis.
f.clause: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver (item 7, frequency)
f.applicability: Products 3 years or less from U.S. approval date
f.exceptions: FDA grants or denies on an application-specific basis

FDA will grant or deny the request on an application-specific basis.
rows.location: III.B. Applicants Without a PSUR Waiver (item 7, frequency)

f.title: Submit the PBRER less often only with an annual report in another accepted format
f.statement: Where more than 3 years have passed since U.S. approval, applicants can alternatively submit a PBRER less frequently than annually on the condition that they also submit an annual periodic safety report in one of the other acceptable formats (PADER/PAER or PSUR) as needed to fulfil the annual requirement.
